title: Fourteen Springs and One Short Hem
subtitle: 服装与礼仪 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 服装与礼仪（人与社会·历史社会与文化）
meta: 主题语境：服装与礼仪（人与社会·历史社会与文化）　|　核心词汇：dress　|　正文 343 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 dress 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1952 my mother ① made a dress that no guest in the town would have worn, and she said the making was the whole of the spring. The ② dress, meaning the garment and not the code, ran fourteen springs and stayed unnamed in the book; a dress, she said, is the only thing in a town that is judged by how long it is left unworn.

Every ③ dress in that town had the same short hem at the end of it, and the ④ dress at the end, meaning the one they kept for the wedding and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A dress, my aunt said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to wear; my mother said the wearing is the part that fills fourteen springs.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the dress was the whole of the story, meaning the code and not the garment. The ⑥ dress, meaning the code and not any of that, is the only thing in a story that everybody observes and nobody explains; dress, he said, is either something you make or the only word that means both a garment and a code. He said the code is the part they remember.

By 1961 the ⑦ dress had become a line in a list, and the list had become an argument about the short hem. The ⑧ dress of the whole thing, my mother wrote in April, was one town and fourteen springs of wearing; dress, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to wear. She said the wearing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ dress I remember is the one named in the list, which was given away in 1973 and is still described as the quietest in the town. A ⑩ dress, my aunt said in 1975, is the only one that improves by being worn; every dress, she said, is a code that has agreed to look like a garment. She said the code was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 连衣裙；衣服（指那个镇子里缝就的那一条）
B. n. 连衣裙；衣服（指那件衣服本身，与着装规矩相对）
C. 固定搭配：make a dress 做一条裙子
D. n. 连衣裙；衣服（指留给婚礼穿的那一条）
E. n. 连衣裙；衣服（抽象总称，指一家人的穿衣之事）
F. n. 连衣裙；衣服（指清单上写到、被列名的那一条）
G. n. 着装；着装规矩（指故事里人人都讲究却无人说明的那样东西）
H. n. 着装规矩（抽象总称，指人人都讲究却无人说明的那种规矩）

items.q: made a dress that no guest in the town would have worn
The dress, meaning the garment and not the code
the dress was the whole of the story
the dress had become a line in a list
The dress of the whole thing
A dress, my aunt said in 1975

answers.why: make a dress 意为“做一条裙子”，1952 年母亲做了一条镇子上没有一位客人肯穿的裙子。
dress 意为“连衣裙、衣服”，指那件衣服本身而不是着装规矩，它经过了十四个春天而在簿子上没有名字。
dress 意为“连衣裙、衣服”，指那个镇子上的每一条裙子，每一条下摆都有同一道短短的折边。
dress 意为“连衣裙、衣服”，指留给婚礼穿的那一条，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
dress 意为“着装、着装规矩”，指故事里人人都讲究却无人说明的那样东西，叔叔说这着装规矩就是那个故事的全部。
dress 意为“着装规矩”，指人人都讲究却无人说明的那种规矩而不是那件衣服，是故事里人人都讲究、却无人说明的东西。
dress 意为“连衣裙、衣服”，指清单上写到、被列名的那一条，到 1961 年这条裙子成了清单里的一行。
dress 意为“连衣裙、衣服”，母亲四月写道，整件事的穿衣之事是一个镇子和十四个春天的穿着。
dress 意为“连衣裙、衣服”，我记得的是清单上列名的那一条，1973 年送人了，至今仍被说成镇子里最安静的一条。
dress 为抽象总称，姑姑 1975 年说，一条裙子是唯一会因为被好好穿着而变得更好的东西。
